\begin{bankq}[id=TOPS02-P2-PHY-S2-Q06, source={TOPS - Test 02 (28 Aug 2022)}, paper=2, qno=6, type=numerical, subtopic={Units and dimensions}, answer={6.50}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: dimensional analysis, numerical constants | steps: powers of h, c and r by dimensions; formula for the force per area; substitute the values; solve for k | Casimir force}]

If the force acting on $1\times1$ cm plates separated by 1 $\mu$m is 0.013 dyne, calculate the value of constant $k$ is $P\times10^{-3}$. The value of $P$ is
\end{bankq}

\section*{TMAS papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS04-P1-PHY-S1-Q02, source={TMAS - Test 04 (19 Nov 2023)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=single, subtopic={Errors and measurement}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: errors in a linear fit | steps: slope in terms of tension and density; frequency; propagate the errors}]
In an experiment to study standing waves, you use a string whose mass per length is $\mu=(1.0\pm0.1)\times10^{-4}$ kg/m. You look at the fundamental mode, whose frequency $f$ is related to the length $L$ and tension $T$ of the string by the following equation $L=\dfrac{1}{2f}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$. You make a plot with $L$ on the $y$-axis and $\sqrt T$ on the $x$-axis, and find that the best fitting line is $y=(8.0\pm0.3)\times10^{-3}x+(0.2\pm0.04)$ in SI units. What is the value of the frequency of the wave (including the error)? Express your result in SI unit (Hz).
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$6250\pm859.8$ Hz}
\opt{B}{$1250\pm32.3$ Hz}
\opt{C}{$6250\pm546.9$ Hz}
\opt{D}{$4875\pm287$ Hz}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TMAS04-P1-PHY-S2-Q10, source={TMAS - Test 04 (19 Nov 2023)}, paper=1, qno=10, type=multi, subtopic={Vernier and screw gauge}, answer={B,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: screw gauge reading | steps: zero error from the rotation; reading; corrected thickness}]
The pitch of screw gauge is $1$ mm and its circular scale is divided into $100$ divisions. When nothing is put between the studs the zero of main scale is not seen, but when circular scale is rotated by $450^\circ$ the zero of main scale is seen and the zero of main scale coincide with the zero of circular scale. When a glass plate is placed between the studs, the circular scale lies between $18^{\mathrm{th}}$ to $19^{\mathrm{th}}$ division of main scale and circular scale reads $34$ divisions. Then,
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Error is positive zero error and its magnitude is $1.25$ mm.}
\opt{B}{Error is negative zero error and its magnitude is $1.25$ mm.}
\opt{C}{The thickness of the glass plate is $19.59$ mm.}
\opt{D}{The thickness of the glass plate is $17.09$ mm.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
